Analyzing Self-Hosted Options

Gemini said

It’s a golden age for self-hosted dashboards, but I totally get why you might be looking for a change. While Homepage is beloved for its sleek YAML-based configuration, sometimes you want a visual editor, less "codey" setup, or just a different aesthetic.

Here are the best alternatives for wrangling your Docker containers into a beautiful startpage.

1. Homarr: The Modern Heavyweight

If Homepage feels a bit too "manual" because of the YAML files, Homarr is likely your next stop. It’s snappy, modern, and features a full drag-and-drop UI.

  • Best for: People who want a GUI instead of editing text files.

  • Key Feature: High-level Docker integration. It can start/stop containers directly from the dashboard and shows real-time resource stats without much fuss.

  • Vibe: Professional, polished, and very "SaaS-looking."

2. Dashy: The Feature King

Dashy is for the person who wants to customize every single pixel. It is arguably the most feature-rich dashboard out there, though it can be a bit overwhelming at first.

  • Best for: Power users and "tinkerers."

  • Key Feature: Over 50 built-in widgets (weather, crypto, system stats) and a massive library of themes. It also supports multiple search engines and status monitoring.

  • Vibe: "The Swiss Army Knife." It does everything, but you might cut yourself on the options.

3. Heimdall: The Simple Classic

Heimdall is the "old reliable" of the bunch. It doesn't try to be a system monitor; it just wants to be a clean set of bookmarks for your apps.

  • Best for: Minimalists who just want to click an icon and go.

  • Key Feature: "Enhanced Pins." For supported apps (like Plex or Pi-hole), it can pull in small bits of data (like "number of active clients") without any complex setup.

  • Vibe: Clean, simple, and "set it and forget it."

4. Flame: The Minimalist’s Dream

Flame is incredibly lightweight and stays out of your way. It’s perfect if you’re running your stack on a lower-powered device like an older Raspberry Pi.

  • Best for: Users who want a fast, "blink-and-you-miss-it" load time.

  • Key Feature: Built-in "Applications" and "Bookmarks" editors directly in the browser. It also has a very handy "Search" bar that works instantly.

  • Vibe: Very Zen. Lots of white space and thin lines.

5. Organizr: The Tabbed Powerhouse

Organizr isn't exactly a "dashboard" in the traditional sense; it’s more of a frontend that wraps your other apps in tabs using iframes.

  • Best for: People who hate having 20 browser tabs open for their server.

  • Key Feature: It allows you to use your services (like Sonarr, Radarr, or Tautulli) inside the Organizr window.

  • Vibe: A "Command Center" feel.

Quick Comparison

FeatureHomarrDashyHeimdallFlame
Config StyleGUI / Drag-and-dropYAML or GUIGUIGUI
ComplexityMediumHighLowLow
Docker IntegrationExcellentGoodBasicBasic
Resource UsageModerateHighLowVery Low

Which one should you pick?

  • If you're tired of YAML: Go with Homarr.

  • If you want a dashboard that looks like a cyberpunk terminal: Go with Dashy.

  • If you just want five buttons that work: Go with Heimdall.
